# Scoping: is θ=π *generated*, not inserted?

**Date:** 2026-07-13 · **Status:** scope / plan only (no implementation). The last
instantiation-level conditional behind the conceptual chain.

## 1. What rests on this, and the precise claim

Two conceptual-phase results leaned on **θ=π**:

- the vorton is a **spin-½ fermion** (Finkelstein–Rubinstein / Wilczek–Zee: θ=π is
  the fermion point);
- **electric-charge quantisation** via the Witten effect `Q = e(n + θm/2π)`, whose
  dyon spectrum `Q = e(n + m/2)` uses θ=π.

**The conditional:** is θ=π *forced by the substrate*, or a free input we chose to
match the fermion requirement? If forced → those results are genuinely derived; if
it must be inserted → they are assumptions. This scoping asks what it would take to
settle that, honestly including the ways it can fail.

## 2. The mechanism (established)

A topological θ-term acquires a *definite, quantised* coefficient by **integrating
out a gapped fermionic sector coupled to the order parameter**. The rigorous
template is **Abanov–Wiegmann** (*Nucl. Phys. B* 570 (2000) 685,
[hep-th/9911025](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9911025)): integrating out `N` Dirac
fermions gapped by the sigma-model field yields **Θ = Nπ**. So:

> **θ=π ⟺ an *odd* number of Dirac fermions in the microscopic sector.**

This is the same physics as a topological-insulator surface (a single Dirac cone →
θ=π magnetoelectric response) and, in a monopole background, the **Jackiw–Rebbi**
zero mode → induced charge **±½** (*Phys. Rev. D* 13 (1976) 3398) — i.e. the θ=π
Witten half-charge. The coefficient is a **spectral-asymmetry index** of the Dirac
operator: quantised, not tunable. That is exactly the property we need — *if* the
right fermion exists.

## 3. The pivotal fork (and the one-substrate tension)

Two honest sub-questions decide everything:

**(a) Is θ=π already the same Z₂ we have, or independent?** The vorton's fermionic
character came from `π₁(RP²)=Z₂` (FR / Volovik–Mineev). θ=π is *also* a Z₂ (mod 2π)
statement. If these are the **same** topological fact, θ=π is near-automatic given
the nematic grain (and tests 1–3 + FR essentially settle it). If **independent**,
θ=π needs its own microscopic origin (a Dirac sector). Distinguishing these is the
first task — and the answer is not obvious.

**(b) Does the substrate *provide* the fermion, or must one be *added*?** Abanov–
Wiegmann needs a Dirac fermion to integrate out. Two routes:

- **Intrinsic (one-substrate-respecting, the target).** The fermion is the
  substrate's **own emergent excitation** — e.g. the **CP¹ spinon** (`n = z†σz`,
  with `z` a fractionalised excitation of the director). If the substrate's spinon
  sector is a *single Dirac* fermion, integrating it out gives θ=π with **no new
  fundamental field**. This connects to real physics (deconfined criticality,
  θ-terms in quantum antiferromagnets).
- **Added (ontology cost).** Postulating a separate fundamental fermion generates θ
  but introduces a **second fundamental field**, straining "one substrate" (D2).
  Acceptable only as a fallback, and it would *downgrade* the north-star claim.

**The crux:** does the nematic RP²/3D substrate yield an *odd, intrinsic* Dirac
sector? Plausible, not guaranteed.

## 4. Work packages

**WP-A — analytic (the real derivation).** Carry out the Abanov–Wiegmann gradient
expansion for a Dirac fermion gapped by the RP²/3D director; show the induced term
is Θ=Nπ and **identify N from the substrate's own content** (ideally the CP¹
spinon). Deliverable: θ=Nπ with N fixed intrinsically. *Pen-and-paper + symbolic
(sympy); research-scale; genuine uncertainty.*

**WP-B — numeric could-fail check (buildable now, extends test 3).** Put a lattice
Dirac operator in the **hedgehog background already constructed in
`instantiation/emergent_magnetic.py`**, diagonalise, and check for the **Jackiw–
Rebbi zero mode → induced charge ½**. A clean, falsifiable test that a *single*
Dirac fermion in the emergent-monopole background realises the θ=π half-charge.
Deliverable: induced charge ≈ ½ (PASS) or not (FAIL). *~150–250 lines; one session;
builds directly on test 3.*

Recommended order: **WP-B first** (concrete, could-fail, reuses test 3), then WP-A
to establish whether N is *forced* intrinsically.

## 5. Pre-registered criteria + anti-drift guard

- **PASS.** An intrinsic (substrate-emergent) **odd** Dirac sector is identified,
  and WP-B yields induced charge ½ → **θ=π is generated, not inserted**; the fermion
  and charge-quantisation results become fully derived.
- **PARTIAL.** θ=Nπ is generated but the parity `N` is an *input* not forced by the
  substrate → θ=π is a **motivated choice, not forced**; the dependent results are
  honestly downgraded from "derived" to "derived given one input."
- **FAIL / STALL.** No consistent intrinsic fermion sector, or the induced term is
  θ=0/2π (boson) → the fermion + charge results **lose their structural footing**,
  putting them in tension with the FR-derived fermion and forcing a rethink.

**Anti-drift guard (critical).** `N` must be **fixed by the substrate's field
content**, never tuned to land on π. If we ever find ourselves choosing N=1
*because we need θ=π*, that is calibration — forbidden (D1/D4). The entire value of
this step is that N is *forced*.

## 6. Honest risk assessment

Unlike tests 1–3 — pure topology, guaranteed to pass if the math is right — **this
step can genuinely fail to resolve.** Three realistic outcomes: (i) θ=π forced
intrinsically (a real capstone); (ii) θ=π requires an added or input ingredient
(partial, with an ontology or honesty cost); (iii) ambiguous — the substrate's
fermion content isn't cleanly defined without further modelling choices (a stall).
All three are acceptable *outcomes*; only pretending (i) when we have (ii)/(iii)
would be drift.

This is also where the program stops being "compute an invariant of a given field"
and becomes "posit dynamics and integrate out matter" — a materially larger,
more open-ended kind of step, with correspondingly wider error bars.

## 7. What I'd need to proceed

- **For WP-B:** nothing new — extend `emergent_magnetic.py` with a lattice Dirac

- **For WP-A:** a decision on the microscopic ansatz for the substrate's fermionic

Recommendation: if pursued, do **WP-B** as the next concrete increment (it is
could-fail and reuses existing code), and treat **WP-A** as a separate,
research-scale undertaking with explicitly wider uncertainty.

# WP-A: the *origin* of θ=π — is it forced by the substrate?

**Date:** 2026-07-13 · **Status:** analytic result (conceptual, not numeric).
Follows the [θ scope](theta-generation-scope-2026-07-13.md) and WP-B (mechanism
verified). This is the honest edge of the program.

## The question

WP-B showed the *mechanism*: an odd (single) Dirac cone in the hedgehog gives the
Jackiw–Rebbi ½ = θ=π. WP-A asks the *origin*: does the substrate **force** an odd
Dirac sector, so θ=π is generated rather than inserted?

## Result A — θ=π is not an independent knob (positive, real)

θ=π and "the vorton is a fermion" are the **same Z₂**, stated in two languages:

- Finkelstein–Rubinstein: `π₁` of configuration space has a Z₂ generator
  (2π-rotation = exchange) → fermionic quantisation.
- Wilczek–Zee: the soliton's statistics is `J = θ/2π`; **θ=π ⟺ fermion**, θ=0 ⟺
  boson.

So θ mod 2π *is* the statistics. Having (in the conceptual phase) tied the vorton's
statistics to `π₁(RP²)=Z₂`, **θ=π is locked to that same invariant — it is not a
free parameter and was never tuned.** Given a fermionic vorton, θ=0 is *forbidden*.
This is a genuine tightening: θ=π is an *equivalent restatement* of a derived
result, not an extra assumption.

## Result B — but the fermionic (odd) class itself is *not generic* (the honest limit)

To *generate* θ via Abanov–Wiegmann you need a fermionic sector to integrate out,
and Θ = N·π, so θ=π needs **N odd**. Whether the substrate supplies an odd Dirac
sector is a **microscopic choice the director ontology does not fix**, and — the
sharp point — the *standard* fractionalisation does **not** give it:

- **Bosonic route (NCCP¹):** bosonic spinons + a noncompact U(1); no fermion to
  integrate out. The θ/WZW content comes from Berry phases (Haldane, θ ~ 2πS).
- **Fermionic route (the dual):** the standard Néel–VBS fermionic dual is an SU(2)
  gauge theory with **N_f = 2** two-component Dirac fermions — an **even** number →
  Θ = 2π ≡ 0 → a **bosonic** soliton.

So a *natural* microscopic completion of a 3-vector order parameter tends to land in
the **even / θ=0 / bosonic** class — the **opposite** of what the program needs.

*Numerically confirmed* (`instantiation/theta_parity.py`, extending WP-B): N_f
decoupled cones in the hedgehog bind N_f zero modes → induced charge N_f/2, so
N_f=1 → ½ (fermion, θ=π), **N_f=2 → 1 (boson, θ=0)**, N_f=3 → 3/2 (fermion). Parity
is what matters, and the standard N_f=2 dual is a boson.

## The deep finding — a consistency requirement with a real risk of tension

Putting A and B together, honestly:

- The whole fermion + charge-quantisation edifice **requires** the substrate to sit
  in the **odd-Dirac / θ=π** class.
- Result A says that *within* that class θ=π is locked to the fermion (no tuning) —
  good.
- But Result B says that class is **non-generic**, and a natural completion gives
  the **even / θ=0 / bosonic** alternative, which would make the vorton a *boson* —
  **contradicting the FR-derived fermion and collapsing the charge-quantisation
  chain.**

**This also qualifies the conceptual-phase fermion result.** Finkelstein–Rubinstein
shows fermionic quantisation is *allowed* by `π₁(RP²)=Z₂`; θ=π is what *selects* it.
So "the vorton **is** a fermion" was really "**can be**, and **is** iff the
substrate is in the odd/θ=π class." That class is assumed, non-generic, and could
fail. WP-A therefore **lowers** confidence in the fermion and charge-quantisation
results by exposing the dynamical conditional they carry.

## Net status of the θ=π conditional

- **Mechanism:** verified (WP-B).
- **Not a free knob:** verified (Result A — θ=π ≡ the FR fermion Z₂).
- **Forced by the substrate:** **NO — not established, and non-generic.** A natural
  completion gives even/θ=0/bosonic, which would break the chain. **Origin
  unresolved, with a flagged vulnerability.**

Honest label: **PARTIAL, with a genuine risk of failure** — better than WP-B's
"mechanism only," short of closure, and it *reduces* rather than inflates the
standing of the dependent results. Reporting it otherwise would be exactly the
overclaim (D1) this re-anchoring exists to prevent.

## What would actually settle it (and could come out negative)

A concrete microscopic model of *this* substrate whose fractionalisation is
**provably odd-Dirac (θ=π)** — a real research programme with a real chance of a
**negative** result (that the nematic generically fractionalises bosonic/even, θ=0,
making vortons bosons). Until then the fermion/charge results stand **only under the
assumed odd/θ=π class**, which must be stated wherever they are used.

## Anti-drift

No parameter was tuned to π (Result A makes π structural given fermions). The
even/θ=0 risk (Result B) is surfaced, not buried — the honest thing is to carry the
"odd-class assumption" as an explicit, non-generic condition on the whole edifice.

**Sources:** [Abanov–Wiegmann, θ-terms in NLSMs (hep-th/9911025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9911025) ·
[Deconfined criticality: symmetries & dualities, PRX 7 (2017) 031051](https://journals.aps.org/prx/pdf/10.1103/PhysRevX.7.031051)
(bosonic CP¹ vs the N_f=2 fermionic dual).

# Proposal: Re-anchoring the RS modelling programme on topological-soliton mathematics

**Status:** frontier proposal · **Date:** 2026-07-11 · **Claim discipline:** nothing
here is asserted as settled; this document fixes an *objective* and a *first
could-fail test*, not a result.

**Companion to the books:** faithful to *The Relational Substrate* (technical
volume, Ch. 13 Primary Topology, Ch. 17–19 Vortons, Part VIII Operations) and
*Coherent Biblical Ontology — Bachelor's Edition* (Ch. 5 Vortons, Ch. 8 Motion/
Light/Electricity/Magnetism, Axiom M1). Where the two are quoted below, the
wording is theirs.

---

## 0. Why this document exists (the drift finding)

The prior modelling core (`src/model.js` + the resilience/regime layer) is
**retired as the programme's spine**, for a reason the project's own record
already states plainly:

- Against static physical observables (refractive index, molecular geometry,
  peroxide torsion) *"the grammar is **calibrated**, not used to derive a
  prediction. Result: consistency at best, never novel evidence"*
  (`relational-substrate-validation-status.md`).
- The refractive-index success *"is the established Shannon–Fischer 2016 method,
  so the pass is consistency with established crystal chemistry, not independent
  evidence."*
- From there the programme **pivoted to a path-dependent order effect** (gentle-
  first "coaxing" resilience) and pursued it across metal fatigue, cardiac
  preconditioning, wildfire, and stress-psychology.

That pivot is **objective drift**. The stated outcome was *a mathematically
plausible substrate model of atoms, molecules, light, electricity and
magnetism*. The stress-history / resilience programme optimised instead for *a
novel prediction that beats a statistical null* — a different objective the model
substituted for the stated one. The order-effect work is therefore declared
**out of scope** here. It is archived, not deleted, and may be revisited only as
an incidental downstream effect, never as the north star.

The diagnosis of *why* the old core could only ever calibrate: it is a
first-order **linear-response** form — coherence is an affine blend of the five
grammar sliders, and all history/memory enters as ±3–12% multiplicative nudges.
Such a form recovers the *direction* of effects and never their *magnitude* or
*structure*. It is the wrong mathematics for a substrate whose primitives are
**topological**.

---

## 1. The locked objective (north star — the anti-drift anchor)

> **A single relational substrate in which the *vorton* (primary topology) is the
> sole structural primitive, and matter (secondary topology), light, electricity
> and magnetism are its downstream expressions — with electricity and magnetism
> treated as complementary modes of one substrate, not as independent forces.**

Three commitments make this an *anchor* rather than a slogan:

1. **Only the vorton is structural.** Per the ontology, *light = Operation A
   (propagation)*, *electricity = Operation B (reconfiguration)*, *magnetism =
   Operation C (alignment)*, *vorton = Operation D (closure formation)*. Of these
   only D yields a stable identity-bearing structure. Charge is explicitly *"a
   directional bias… derivative in explanatory status, real in consequence, **and
   not a substance**."* Any model that promotes a field description (E, B, a
   bivector) to structural rank has **drifted** and must be corrected. *(This
   corrects an earlier suggestion in the design discussion to anchor on Geometric
   Algebra's E+IB bivector — that inverts the hierarchy: it makes E&M structural,
   which the ontology forbids.)*
2. **Success = structural reproduction of known physics from one substrate**, not
   novelty. Re-deriving an established quantity *parameter-free from the vorton*
   is a win, not the dead end the prior cycle judged it to be.
3. **Ontology before model** (the books' own discipline). The mathematics below is
   a *language and instantiation* for the vorton; it does not reduce the ontology
   to itself.

---

## 2. The corrected substrate anchor: topological-soliton / knot-field theory

The vorton is defined as *"a stable torsional knot-state of the relational
substrate… identity carried topologically rather than materially,"* with
invariants that are *"closure class, winding relations, linking structure… a
stability envelope."* The mathematics that speaks exactly this language is
**topological-soliton theory**, and its lineage is the vorton's own:

- **Kelvin's vortex atom (1867)** — atoms as knotted vortex tubes in a continuous
  medium: the literal ancestor of "vorton," and the seed of both knot theory and
  modern solitons.
- **Skyrme model** — particles (baryons) as **topological solitons of a
  continuous field**, classified by an *integer* topological charge. Precedent
  that particle properties can be *derived* from a knot in a continuum.
- **Hopfions** — closed, twisted, **toroidal** solitons whose identity *is* an
  integer **Hopf / linking number**, *topologically protected under continuous
  deformation* (= the book's **stability envelope**), now realised experimentally
  in magnets and in light.

**The ontological rank is preserved, not dissolved.** The technical volume
already refuses to reduce the vorton to a soliton ("*ontologically stronger… not
merely any persistent pattern*"). That stands: topological-soliton theory
supplies the vorton's **equations and invariants**; RS supplies the claim that
this knot-state is *primary* and that matter is constituted from it.

**Where Geometric Algebra re-enters — one tier down.** GA is a *local* language
of rotation and orientation. It is the wrong tool for the *structure* (a global,
topological fact) but the right tool for the *downstream derivation*: once a
vorton exists, GA is the natural language for computing how its circulation
*expresses* as Operations A/B/C, and how a transient (light) interacts with it.
So the split is:

| Half of the north star | Mathematics |
|---|---|
| The vorton *structure* (Operation D output) | topological-soliton / knot-field theory (Kelvin → Skyrme → Hopfion) |
| The *downstream* lanes (light A, electricity B, magnetism C) from the vorton's circulation | Geometric Algebra, layered on top |

---

## 3. The RS ↔ mathematics mapping (faithful to both books)

A hopfion carries **two linked circulations** (toroidal and poloidal). RS already
names E and M as **complementary** modes — the book's resonance chapter pairs
*capacitive (stored disequilibrium, Op B)* with *inductive (held alignment, Op
C)*. The two linked circulations are the natural structural home for that
complementarity:

| RS ontology | Book wording | Topological-soliton reading |
|---|---|---|
| **Vorton** (primary topology, Op D) | "stable torsional knot-state… identity carried topologically" | a **hopfion-class** soliton; identity = **Hopf/linking invariant** + stability envelope |
| **Magnetism** (Op C) | *"static torsional equilibrium — a held twist-geometry"*; polarity = *"opposite chirality of the same held configuration"*; dissipates no energy (held geometry, not activity) | the **held twist** of the soliton; **polarity = sign/handedness of the linking number** (a static topological chirality — hence no dissipation) |
| **Electricity** (Op B) | reconfiguration; voltage = torsional disequilibrium; current = coherent reseating of a vorton lattice; charge = derivative asymmetry | the **dynamic reconfiguration/slip** mode; **charge magnitude = the integer topological charge** |
| **E & M complementary** | capacitive ↔ inductive resonance between "complementary forms of ordered constraint" | the two **linked circulations** (dynamic flow ↔ static held twist) of one soliton |
| **Light** (Op A) | transient, "open, coherent, route-bearing, unwindable" | a **non-topological** propagating excitation of the same substrate; light–vorton coupling = the existing **admissibility** walkthroughs (salvaged) |
| **Matter** (secondary topology) | lattices/interfaces from coupled vortons | multi-soliton **coupling** regimes; molecules = bound hopfion complexes |

**The sandbox already gropes toward this.** `closedForms = ['circle','trefoil',
'double']` are knot/link classes (unknot, trefoil, link); the six identity
metrics (closure/return/boundedness/coherence/reseating/leakage) are *heuristic
stand-ins* for a topological invariant. The core upgrade is to **replace the
hand-tuned identity-score with a genuine invariant (Hopf / linking number)** —
the same move that ends the "calibrated, not derived" problem.

---

## 4. Anti-drift discipline (carried over, sharpened)

- **Parameter-free or it doesn't count.** The failure mode to avoid is per-case
  calibration. A prediction that needs a fitted coefficient is not a derivation.
- **Pre-register every test** (success *and* failure criteria) before running it —
  the one genuinely valuable habit inherited from the prior cycle.
- **Structural reproduction of known physics is the objective**, not a novel
  null-beating effect. Reproducing charge quantisation from a linking number is a
  *win*.
- **Confidence stays capped** until a parameter-free quantitative reproduction
  lands in a domain no established theory already covers, or a known quantity is
  reproduced with genuinely no free handles.
- **The data-access wall is real** (numerically-extractable held-out data is
  scarce) and is a first-class project risk, not an excuse.

---

## 5. First pre-registered could-fail test

**Claim under test:** *charge is quantised because it is a topological (linking)
invariant of the vorton — an integer — and magnetic polarity is the sign of that
same invariant.*

- **Setup:** instantiate a vorton as a hopfion-class configuration of a single
  continuous substrate field; compute its **Hopf/linking invariant** directly
  from the configuration (no fitted parameter).
- **Prediction A (charge):** admissible stable configurations carry **integer**
  topological charge; there is no stable fractional-charge vorton in the base
  species. Success = discreteness falls out of the topology, not a threshold we
  tuned.
- **Prediction B (polarity):** reversing the **handedness** of the held twist
  flips the sign of the invariant and nothing else — reproducing *"north and
  south as opposite chirality of the same held configuration"* with **no
  additional structure**.
- **Precedent that this is not fantasy:** the Skyrme model already yields integer
  baryon number as a topological charge.
- **Failure criterion (stated in advance):** if stable configurations require a
  tuned parameter to land on integers, or if polarity reversal demands structure
  beyond a sign flip of the invariant, the mapping is falsified at the first rung
  and we say so.

Only if this rung holds do we climb: two coupled vortons → a bond quantity;
light (transient) admissibility against a vorton of known invariant; then a
secondary-topology (molecule) quantity — each pre-registered, each parameter-free.

---

## 6. Salvage / archive ledger

| Keep | Archive (out of scope) | Retire |
|---|---|---|
| The **objective** (§1), the **pre-registration discipline**, the **five-operation** typology, the **knot-class vocabulary** (`closedForms`), the **admissibility** walkthroughs for light–vorton coupling, the **physics target list** in `research/` | The **order-effect / resilience / regime** programme and its cross-domain directional ledger (real work, wrong objective) | The **linear-response core** as the programme spine (`calculateOutcome`'s affine coherence + ±10% memory nudges) — superseded by an invariant-based core |

---

## 7. Open questions (honest frontier)

1. **Species spectrum.** Does a *single* substrate field admit a hopfion spectrum
   whose invariants match a recognisable particle inventory — or only one species?
2. **Continuum → known constants.** Can any established constant (a mass or charge
   *ratio*, a g-factor) emerge parameter-free, or does the substrate need
   additional structure (and if so, is that structure still "one substrate")?
3. **Molecules as secondary topology.** Is there *any* bond quantity that coupled
   hopfions reproduce without calibration? (This is where the prior cycle only
   ever calibrated.)
4. **What GA actually buys.** Does layering GA on top yield the E/M expressions
   *derivationally*, or is it re-description?

---

## 8. Next steps

1. This document = the locked objective + first test (done).
2. Decide the substrate field for the hopfion instantiation (candidate: a
   Faddeev–Niemi / unit-vector field admitting Hopf solitons) — a small,
   pre-registered numerical experiment computing the linking invariant of one
   stable configuration.
3. Wire the invariant computation as the **new identity core**, replacing the
   heuristic identity-score, and re-express the sandbox's knot-classes as its
   base species.

No code beyond the single invariant experiment until Prediction A/B (§5) has been
attempted and honestly scored.

**Programme id:** GT. **Branch:** `research/gravity-time-admissibility`. **Base:** `22e252e560cc711d337b6ae506b0fb76728247d6`, the closed and reviewed Generation 8G head of the Constraint Laboratory (formal integration). The base choice is justified in [`docs/reuse-map.md`](docs/reuse-map.md) §1.

**Method (from GT-P002, 2026-10-14):** Open-Thetical Research, OTR 1.0, [`../research-methods/open-thetical-research.md`](../research-methods/open-thetical-research.md), sha256 `2d902395…88dd`. Adoption notes and the cross-branch sharing route are in [`../research-methods/README.md`](../research-methods/README.md). GT-P002's input is [`provenance/prompts/GT-P002-agent-input.md`](provenance/prompts/GT-P002-agent-input.md). The governance in §5 below is unchanged; OTR adds recursive round selection on top of it.

## 1. Question

Can a minimal architecture of relational constraints, acting through constrained stochastic actualisation, produce both of the following?

1. Behaviour resembling gravitational attraction: a stable relational basin toward which relational distance tends.
2. Systematic differences in the relative progression of recurrent processes, analogous to gravitational clock-rate differences.

Can both arise from one constraint architecture, without imposing the equations or mechanisms that describe them? And does the same architecture help explain spatial ordering, distance, direction and temporal succession?

The programme is not asked to prove the Relational Substrate. It asks what follows from its proposals, where they are coherent, where they need refinement, and whether their explanatory reach extends this far. A model that cannot produce gravitational behaviour is a result.

## 2. Commitments inherited from the CBO v2.4 baseline

These are taken from `books/v2/analysis/research-baseline.md` and Appendix E on `main` at `84ae9a4`. They are not revised here.

- Relational primacy is the governing proposal.
- T0 names whatever conditions actualisation. Its deeper ontology is open.
- T1 is actualised, history-bearing relational order.
- Constrained stochastic actualisation is a working hypothesis.
- Admissibility (forbidding) and tendency (favouring) are distinct.
- T-C-R is the candidate grammar of consequential relation.
- Substrate spatiality is unresolved: intrinsic, emergent and proto-spatial families are all live.
- Time as the ordering of actualisation is a working ontological interpretation, not a temporal theory.
- A fundamental limit or constraint on primitive event succession is an open candidate.
- **Design is an upstream premise of the programme, not an outcome.** No model result is offered as evidence for or against it.

Historical mechanisms are not canonised. Substrate tension, closure knots and a universal cadence are preserved only as candidate interpretations in the register ([`hypotheses.md`](hypotheses.md)).

## 3. Model class and declared scaffolding

The programme starts inside the existing grammar: the O=2 pair-relation model of the Constraint Laboratory, on N labelled entities with C(N,2) binary relations, single-toggle dynamics and the ordinary rule DSL. A rule's weight multiplies the weight of one toggle, and `prohibit` is the zero. Before any new primitive or expressivity axis is added, the register asks whether the existing grammar can represent the behaviour (CL-T12 already guarantees current-state weight universality with unbounded factors). The scientific question is therefore **which minimal, label-covariant, relation-reading rules** produce a basin, not whether some rule set can be written to produce one.

Anything imposed is declared as scaffolding. It is never presented as emergent.

| Scaffold | Where it is used | What it is not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Held source**: a designated set of entities whose mutual relations are prohibited from dissolving | Basin rounds | Not mass and not a gravitating body. It is a fixed relational structure against which a tendency can be measured |
| **Relational distance**: shortest-path length in the current pair graph | Observable only | Not a primitive metric. It is a derived function of the current relations, and no rule reads it |
| **Global event count** (jump-chain clock) | Step-indexed quantities | Not a universal clock. A second convention, continuous time with per-slot rates, is always reported beside it |
| **Labelled entities** and a finite N | Everywhere | Not physical particles. N is a resource bound |

Rules are **label-covariant templates**. A template is instantiated identically over every ordered witness, so no rule names a direction, a source or a place. A template instantiated per witness multiplies once per satisfying witness. That is declared semantics, and it is distinct from duplicating syntax.

## 4. Candidates

All of the following are candidates. None is privileged for resembling familiar physics.

- **D**, directional tendency: weights make some trajectories preferentially realised.
- **A**, asymmetric pathway availability: the admissible future pathways change, and a tendency may appear without any directional instruction.
- **A→D**, emergent tendency from admissibility: hard or soft restriction of pathways produces a statistical directional bias.
- **U**, unified gravitational-temporal constraint: the configuration that produces a basin also changes the accessibility, coordination or frequency of recurrent actualisations.
- **Additional candidates and artefacts** are listed in the register: coordination-mediated tendency; clock-convention dependence; density and boundary artefacts.

## 5. Governance

The laboratory's standards apply in full:

- predeclared and frozen plans, committed and pushed before execution;
- exact small-system analysis where possible;
- deterministic replay, so no seed is needed for exact work;
- symmetry and parameter robustness;
- negative controls;
- null and failed results recorded;
- observation, inference and interpretation kept apart;
- frozen comparison targets.

The programme keeps its own records under `gravity-time/`: plans and journey, reports and tables, provenance, and a coherence ledger in the laboratory's schema. It reads the laboratory's ledgers and the formal catalogue without changing them. Proposals that would change the ontology are written as explicit proposals for later review ([`docs/ontology-proposals.md`](docs/ontology-proposals.md)). The CBO books are not edited.

Pass and fail are reserved for software, CI, validation and execution contracts. No system is ranked by a scalar.

## 3. A reanalysis that needs no new computation

This is a mathematical inference, layer 2. It was made while writing this audit, from the G0 template definitions; no new cell was run. It explains G0 observation O5 and extends it.

**Claim.** Every label-covariant template on the O=2 pair grammar whose condition reads only the two relations joining the toggled pair (a,b) to one witness c is a reversible chain, and its continuous-time stationary law is a triple-local Gibbs law. This holds for form rules, dissolve rules, mixtures of them and any finite composition, in HELD and FREE modes.

**Argument.**
1. For the toggle of relation ab, call the product of all form-rule factors f and the product of dissolve-rule factors d. Per-witness instantiation makes the rate ratio r_ab(x) = f/d a product over c of φ(x_ac, x_bc).
2. Label covariance requires φ(u,v) = φ(v,u), so φ depends only on s = u + v ∈ {0, 1, 2}.
3. Take a potential ψ on vertex triples that depends only on the number k of present relations in the triple. Set ψ(1+s) − ψ(s) = log φ(s). That fixes ψ up to a constant, and H(x) = Σ over triples of ψ(k_triple) satisfies r_ab(x) = exp(H(x+ab) − H(x)) for every pair and state.
4. So Kolmogorov's criterion holds, the chain satisfies detailed balance, and π_ct ∝ exp H.

Because Σ over triples of ψ(k) is a linear combination of edge, wedge and triangle counts, this is exactly G0's O5: π_ct ∝ m^S with S an edge, wedge or triangle count. It generalises to every single-witness K≤3 composition. The HELD scaffold only freezes three coordinates, and that preserves detailed balance on the reachable class. Hard prohibition of a formation restricts the chain to a closed set on which the remaining rates still satisfy the criterion. The general fact, that local Glauber-type dynamics with gradient rate ratios are reversible with exponential-random-graph laws, is standard. The application to this grammar is the new step.

**Consequences for G0/G1, before any new run:**

- **No arrow.** Every G0 and G1 cell is reversible. None can show a stationary probability current, an irreversible-looking event order in stationarity, or oscillatory relaxation; the generator spectrum is real. Lens D (directional tendency) was observable in G0 only as stationary occupancy, never as stationary direction of succession.
- **Kinetic freedom.** G1's finding that CLOSE(m) and HOLD(1/m) share π is a special case: any two compositions with the same r_ab share π_ct. Within this class the stationary law is fixed by the ratio, and everything else is kinetics.
- **Absent literals add nothing new.** An absent literal is 1 − present, so `form(a-b) | absent(a-c)` at factor m is DENS(m^(N−2)) composed with ADJ(1/m). Different syntax, same kernel (CL-T09 Möbius basis).

**Where the class ends.** A template whose condition uses two witnesses in asymmetric roles is not covered. An example is `form(a-b) | present(a-c) & present(c-d)`, with c,d ∉ {a,b} and c ≠ d. Analytically:
- Let P(ab) count, over both endpoints, the 2-paths leaving that endpoint into the rest of the graph.
- Δ_ac P(ab) = #{d : cd present}, while Δ_ab P(ac) = #{d : bd present}.
- These differ whenever deg(c) and deg(b) differ outside {a,b,c}.
- So the elementary square (x, x+ab, x+ab+ac, x+ac) has non-unit cycle affinity, and the chain is **not** reversible.

The template is K3, label-covariant and uses only present literals: it is inside the existing grammar.

This identifies the largest untouched region adjacent to G0. It is the boundary between **gradient (potential) dynamics**, which is all G0 explored, and **non-gradient dynamics**, which the grammar admits but no GT cell has entered.

## 5. Lens register used to select E0A

These lenses are kept plural. None is a target.
- **D**, directional tendency.
- **A**, asymmetric admissibility.
- **A→D**, derived tendency.
- **B**, basin by retention.
- **C**, coordination or competing rules.
- **K**, kinetic freedom.
- **E**, emergent source and proximity.
- **X**, artefact families: density, imposed source, boundary, finite-state saturation, clock normalisation, projection, estimator.

One lens is added from §3:

- **R, stationary arrow from non-gradient constraint.** In a stationary state, a directed succession of relational change (cycle currents, event-order asymmetry, complex relaxation modes) arises only when the local rate ratios are not the gradient of any configuration function. R is a mechanism lens. It does not claim that any physical arrow of time is of this kind.

The cross product is 12 family-grades × {HELD, FREE} × {5, 6} = **48 exact cells**.

PATH families use the weak grade only. A K3 two-witness template has 2(N−2)(N−3) witnesses per pair, so the strong grade would multiply rates by up to 4^24 at N=6. Saturation at strong grades was already a G0 finding (O2), and it removes selectivity. This choice is made from witness arithmetic, before any PATH computation.

### Complementarity

The 12 entries form four contrasts:

1. **Gradient against non-gradient** at comparable grade: CLOSE/HOLD/ANTI against PATH.
2. **Formation against retention at equal local ratio**: CLOSE vs HOLD (gradient) and PATHF+ vs PATHH+ (non-gradient). This asks whether the G1 shared-basin identity survives irreversibility.
3. **Cooperating, opposing and competing compositions**: SPLIT, COMPETE and FRUST.
4. **Soft and hard repulsion**: ANTI and EXCL.

HELD against FREE separates scaffold effects from what the rule does unaided.

## What E0 left uncertain

1. **GT-Q07.** Does CSPH's attachment selectivity, together with its stationary arrow, survive as N grows? On published data it is clock-dependent and density-dependent (GT-F34): the continuous margin is +0.046 → +0.009, the jump margin +0.073 → +0.065, and the null-density-standardised continuous margin +0.023 → −0.073.
2. **Handover persistence.** Does the source-relative handover cycle keep its orientation at N=7? It was invariant across all non-gradient cells at N≤6 (GT-F29).
3. **Equal-ratio gap.** Does the occupancy gap between equal-ratio rules (L1 up to 0.49) keep growing?
4. **Hub-frame legibility in FREE.** Is the FREE-mode arrow still visible relative to the emergent hub?
5. **Radial structure (G2) in a non-gradient setting.** Activity and occupancy by shells 1–4.
6. **The new question this review raised.** How much of any N-dependence is the growing witness load of a fixed grade (audit, sections 2–3)?

## Option A — native fixed-grade scale test, HELD N=7

- **Why.** It asks questions 1, 2, 3 and 5 directly, for the same declared model at a new size. It completes the native sequence N = 5, 6, 7.
- **What varies.** N (7, against the published 5 and 6).
- **What is held fixed.** Families and grades (E0B's W4 grades); the HELD scaffold; the start state (source triangle only); both clocks; the class-free, source-relative and hub frames; and every channel in the validation matrix, plus the additions.
- **Cells (8).** CSPH strong_favour+weak_favour, CSPF strong_favour+weak_suppress, CWPH weak_favour+weak_favour, CWPF weak_favour+weak_suppress, PATHF weak_suppress, PATHH weak_favour, NULL, CLOSEW weak_favour; all HELD N7 under W4.
- **What we would see.**
  - Margins in four forms, plus the a/k profile and the normalised margin.
  - Distance distribution and the detached-probe-count distribution.
  - Shell activity in both clocks.
  - Irreversible flux, entropy production and square affinities.
  - Event-order asymmetry and its top patterns, i.e. the handover.
  - Hub structure and the hub-frame arrow.
  - Class tables (144 permutations) and the Gibbs-projection distance.
  - Autocorrelation times, which are new at this size.
  - The engaged witness census.
- **Informative contrasts.**
  - Handover persists while selectivity vanishes in every form: the arrow and the basin separate further.
  - Selectivity persists in the jump clock only: a kinetic, per-event preference with no time-weighted occupancy advantage.
  - Raw margin positive, standardised margin negative: a sparse-regime preference, as at N6.
  - The handover changes orientation or disappears: a new finite-size regime.
  - A probe-only hub becomes common beyond its null rate (0.108 at N7).
  - None of these: the record says so.
- **Possible artefacts left unresolved.** Witness amplification is only measured (engaged census), not controlled. The fall in source share is confounded with N.
- **Cost.** 8 HELD N7 cells. Measured fixture: 136 s and 450 MB per cell for the full pipeline (NULL; CLOSE strong_favour). Extrapolated scientific cells: 2–6 minutes each (feasibility note), so 15–50 minutes for the eight. A 3× margin gives a cap of about 2.5 hours.
- **What next.** An outcome in which "witness amplification" remains the leading candidate would point to option B's bracket as the next round. A handover change would point to mechanism work (GT-Q06).

## Option B — option A plus a within-grammar strength bracket (recommended)

- **Why.** Question 6. Option A alone cannot say whether an N6→N7 change is what a stronger rule would have done at N6.
- **Added cells.** The six non-NULL families of option A, under the existing sensitivity alphabets W3 (all log-factors × 1.585) and W16 (× 2), at N = 5 and 6, all HELD. That is 6 × 2 × 2 = 24 cells, each at most 4,096 states. NULL is alphabet-invariant and is not repeated.
- **Calibration on a step whose ends are already known.**
  - N5-W16 doubles every log-factor, which exactly matches the path-witness maximum from N5 to N6 (12 × 2 = 24).
  - Comparing N5-W16 with the published N6-W4 tests whether "a stronger rule at the smaller size" reproduces the published N5→N6 changes in margin, flux and handover.
  - The test is declared before running and read in both directions: the bracket may or may not explain the published step.
- **What varies.** N at fixed W4 (native sequence), and the alphabet at fixed N (bracket).
- **What is held fixed.** Grades and orderings (W3 and W16 keep both), the scaffold, the start, the clocks and the channels.
- **What we would see.**
  - For each channel, its strength response at N5 and N6 (W4 → W3 → W16).
  - The N=7 native value, and the N=7 engaged log-weight ratio against N6.
- **Informative contrasts.**
  - The N7 change lies within the strength response at N6, in the same direction, and the engaged-load ratio is in the bracketed range: amplification stays a candidate.
  - The N7 change runs opposite to the strength response: amplification is unlikely to be the main cause.
  - The N5-W16 versus N6-W4 calibration fails: the bracket is a poor model of size change even where both ends are known, and the N7 reading must say so.
- **Possible artefacts left unresolved.**
  - The bracket scales closure and path together, so it cannot reproduce the changed closure/path balance of composites. The single-component families (PATHF, PATHH, CLOSEW) are its clean cases.
  - The W3 and W16 kernels are exact Fractions in `build_kernel` but floats in `gtkernel` (relative error 1e-14).
- **Cost.** Option A plus 24 cells of at most 4,096 states. Each takes under 1 minute including GTH-referee-grade checks (N6 HELD validation: under 50 s with the referee, about 1 s without). That adds under 30 minutes.
- **What next.** It separates "the rule got stronger" from "the system got bigger" as far as the grammar allows. Whatever it finds about witness load is the right input to any later decision about a size-normalised family. Such a family would be a grammar change and an ontology proposal; it is not proposed here.

## Option C — mechanism first, no N=7

- **Why.** If the confounds made an N=7 result uninterpretable, a richer N≤6 study might teach more: component ablations of the handover, density-resolved currents, hub persistence in FREE N6 (autocorrelation is now available there), and the W3/W16 bracket alone.
- **Cost.** Small (minutes).
- **What it gives up.** GT-Q07 and G2 at a new size, which are the questions E0 explicitly left open. It also fails to use the machinery built for N=7.
- **Assessment.** The audit shows that most N=7 confounds can be measured or bracketed (identifiability table, audit section 6). Option C's main advantage therefore does not hold. Its components are better folded into option B (bracket) or kept for a later round (ablations, GT-Q06).

## Option D — option B plus a FREE N=7 tranche

- **Why.** Question 4, and the FREE half of every E0 comparison. HELD cannot answer whether organisation emerges without a scaffold.
- **Cells.** FREE N7 NULL, CSPH, PATHH weak_favour and CLOSEW, all under W4. NULL is rerun inside the frozen round as the identity check, although its values are theorem-fixed.
- **Cost.** Measured fixture (FREE N7 NULL, full pipeline): 25 minutes and 3.2 GB. Extrapolated design cells: 30–80 minutes each, so 2–5 hours for the four, run one at a time (`docs/e1-held-free-feasibility.md`).
- **Assessment.** Feasible on this machine within one sitting. It is the only route to the question of unscaffolded emergence at N=7. The cost risk is the iteration-count extrapolation, which is bounded by the cap and the unresolved-cell rule. Two FREE cells at once would fit in memory, but with little margin.

## Recommendation

Option B, with HELD N=7 first. It answers the open E0 questions at a new size. It is the only option that can say anything about effective rule strength, and it does so with instruments the grammar already has. It is expected to take about 1–1.5 hours of computation for HELD and the bracket together.

The FREE tranche (option D) is recommended as a second tranche of the same frozen round, run after HELD under its own 6-hour cap, if several hours of computation are acceptable to the author. Otherwise defer it to a FREE-only round, and take a first look at hub persistence at N=6, where it is now computable in seconds.

Under OTR the choice rests on discrimination, not on the chance of a gravitational-looking result.
- Option B produces several outcome patterns that would each change the next round: arrow without basin, kinetic-only selectivity, sparse-regime selectivity, amplification-explained change, or a new pattern.
- It keeps the negative and fragile channels visible: detachment, standardised margins, null hub rates.
- It removes nothing from the published E0 comparison set.

COMPETE (1,408 iterations at HELD N6) is the slowest published family. It is not proposed for E1. At the same growth it would take about 3,500 iterations per start: about 6 minutes in HELD, or about 1 hour of stationary solving alone in FREE.

**Convergence strategy.**
- Lazy power iteration until the L1 change < 1e-15 and the maximum relative change < 1e-13.
- A second run from a point mass must agree within 1e-10 L1.
- Residual ≤ 1e-12.
- Autocorrelation series to a relative term of 1e-13.
- Cap of 2,000,000 iterations. A cell that hits the cap, or whose starts disagree, is recorded as unresolved, not estimated.
- Saturated cells resolve fine: the relative criterion was designed on them, and reaches 1e-15 relative accuracy on states of probability 1e-12.

**Durability.** The E0 runners write each cell atomically with a `status.json`, and resume by skipping finished cells. An E1 runner would reuse that pattern (`gte0b.run`). A FREE cell of up to about 80 minutes is the unit of loss on interruption.

## 3. What each mode can answer

| Question | HELD N7 | FREE N7 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Does CSPH's source selectivity survive (GT-Q07)? | Yes, directly | No: FREE has no source |
| Does the handover keep its orientation? | Yes, source-relative | Hub-relative only (GT-F28) |
| Radial structure, shells 1–4 (G2) | Yes | No source shells |
| Is the arrow legible relative to an emergent hub? | Hub frame is computed, but the source dominates hubs (null: hub includes a source vertex 89%) | Yes; the question E0B opened |
| Does a centre emerge without a scaffold? | No: a scaffold is imposed | Yes: hub ties, hub persistence (autocorrelation of the hub indicator), class occupancy |
| Equal-ratio occupancy gap | Yes | Yes |

**Neither mode is evidence for the other.** The disappearance of an imposed-source effect in HELD says nothing about unscaffolded organisation. A FREE hub is not a source.

## 4. Recommendation on FREE

FREE N7 is practical but not cheap. Four cells (NULL, CSPH, PATHH weak_favour, CLOSEW) are extrapolated at 2–5 hours of sequential computation with a 3.2 GB peak. Running two at once would fit in memory, but not with much margin.

- **If the FREE tranche is included**, run it after the HELD tranche, under its own wall cap (proposed 6 h). The HELD results are then complete even if FREE is interrupted.
- **If FREE is deferred**, these questions stay open: whether a centre emerges without a scaffold at N=7; whether the hub-frame arrow persists or grows (GT-F28); and how hub ties and hub persistence change with size. They could be asked later as a FREE-only round with the same machinery. They could also be asked at N=6, where autocorrelation and hub persistence are now available, so a cheap first look at hub persistence needs no N=7 computation.

# E1 machinery — vectorised label-covariant template kernel

Step 1 of the E1 recommendation (`docs/roadmap.md`). This is engineering, not a scientific round. No E1 cell has been run, and no E1 plan has been frozen yet.

**Module:** `constraint-lab/src/rs_constraint_lab/gtkernel.py`, version `gt-vectorised-kernel/v1`.
**Tests:** `constraint-lab/tests/test_gtkernel.py`.

## Method

GT templates are label-covariant and multiply once per satisfying witness. So a toggle's weight depends only on witness counts, which are computed for all states at once with bit arithmetic:

| Component | Witness count for pair ab |
| --- | --- |
| closure (form or dissolve) | #{c : x_ac ∧ x_bc} |
| adjacency (form) | #{c : x_ac} + #{c : x_bc} |
| path (form or dissolve) | Σ over end ∈ {a, b} of #{(c, d) : x_end,c ∧ x_c,d}, with c, d ∉ {a, b} and c ≠ d |

- A form component contributes f^w when the relation is absent. A dissolve component contributes g^w when it is present. `prohibit` contributes 0 if w > 0 and 1 otherwise.
- The HELD scaffold zeroes the dissolve weight of the three source relations.
- Rates are computed on the candidate space: all states in FREE, all states containing the source triangle in HELD. The reachable class from the declared start is then found by array breadth-first search.
- The stationary law follows the G0/E0 convention: the jump-chain law by lazy power iteration, then π_ct = π_jump / R. It uses index arrays, with no dense matrix.

## Validation

- **Exact equivalence with `build_kernel`.** Reachable states, transition targets and the full weight array were compared bit for bit, with tolerance 0. W4 weights are powers of two and exact in float64.

  | N | Cells | Mismatches |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | 4 | 36 | 0 |
  | 5 | 36 | 0 |
  | 6 | 36 | 0 (319 s, run once, not in CI) |

  Each N covers all 18 E0A/E0B family-grades in both modes. N=4 and N=5 run in CI. N=6 was run once; its log is `provenance/e1-kernel-n6-validation.log`.
- **Sparse against dense stationary law.** On published E0 cells (CLOSE, PATHF weak_suppress, CSPH and EXCL, HELD N5 and N6), the maximum |Δπ_ct| is at most 4.3e-15 and the residual at most 2.0e-15.

## 3. Numerical findings about the published E0 values

The reproduction found three kinds of fragility in published E0 numbers. None changes a published finding's statement. All are recorded in the ledger as GT-F35. The published tables are unchanged.

1. **Dense LU loses accuracy on improbable states.**
   - **HELD N5 PATHF weak_favour (128 states).** Stationary probabilities reach 1e-12. Measured against an exact rational GTH solve, E0's dense solve had relative errors up to 2.9e-6 there; the new iteration has 6.6e-16.
   - **HELD N6 non-gradient cells.** Probabilities reach 1e-38. The dense solve returned tiny negative values, and E0 clipped them to exactly zero, for 13–136 states per cell.
   - Two consequences:
     - `one_sided_transitions`, published as 120–2,136 in five cells (PATHF, PATHH, CSPF, CWPF, CWPH), is an artefact. Forward flux was positive, but reverse flux from a clipped state was zero. The true value is 0.
     - `attachment_fraction_by_free_edge_count` at densities of stationary mass 1e-14 to 1e-35 is wrong by up to 0.56. Mostly this is k = 9–11; in the saturated cells it is k = 1–8.
   - Wherever `gtobs` and E0 disagree in a cell of ≤4,096 states, a float GTH referee (subtraction-free, positive by construction) decides. In all 15 such cells it agrees with `gtobs`.
   - No published report sentence, finding or hypothesis uses either channel at the affected densities. In particular, the CSPH a/k profile used in the confound audit (k = 1–6) is unaffected; CSPH differs only at k = 11.
2. **L1-stopped iteration leaves rare states unconverged.** E0's FREE N6 cells used lazy iteration stopped on L1 change alone. In the two saturated FREE N6 cells (PATHF weak_favour, PATHH weak_suppress), edge counts 3–10 carry stationary mass from 1e-33 to 1e-17. E0's values of `triangles_given_edge_count` there differ from converged values by up to 67%; E0's law at those states is off by up to 10¹⁵ relative. A strict two-start run (relative change 1e-15 from uniform and from a point mass, agreeing to 1e-15) is the referee for classes above the dense limit, and agrees with `gtobs`. The affected values describe practically unvisited densities and carry no weight in any aggregate.
3. **Tie- and threshold-dependent definitions.** `edge_count_modes` (strict peaks, equal neighbours) and the inclusion threshold of `top_net_currents` (1e-15 × total flux) depend on rounding in E0. `gtobs` keeps the definitions for comparability. The E1 draft proposes reading modes with the tie-aware plateau rule and treating currents below 1e-12 of total flux as zero.

Prompt GT-P003, deliverable 3. This is design analysis, not a scientific round. **No N=7 scientific cell was opened.** Every number below comes from one of three places:

- the NULL family, whose stationary law is uniform by theorem;

## 1. What the representation fixes

The model has one present/absent bit per unordered pair. So there are N(N−1)/2 slots and 2^[N(N−1)/2] FREE configurations. HELD fixes the three source relations, which leaves 2^[N(N−1)/2 − 3] candidates.

| N | Slots | FREE configurations | HELD candidates | Probes (HELD) | Source share of entities |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5 | 10 | 1,024 | 128 | 2 | 0.60 |
| 6 | 15 | 32,768 | 4,096 | 3 | 0.50 |
| 7 | 21 | 2,097,152 | 262,144 | 4 | 0.43 |

These counts are consequences of the chosen representation, and section 7 says what does and does not follow from them.

## 2. Witness counts: definitions, bounds and null means

A label-covariant template multiplies its factor m once per satisfying witness. A component's contribution to a toggle's log-weight is therefore w·log m, where w is the witness count.

| Component | Witnesses of pair ab | Maximum w | N=5 / 6 / 7 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| closure | #{c : x_ac ∧ x_bc} | N−2 | 3 / 4 / 5 |
| adjacency | #{c : x_ac} + #{c : x_bc} | 2(N−2) | 6 / 8 / 10 |
| path | Σ_end #{(c,d) : x_end,c ∧ x_c,d} | 2(N−2)(N−3) | 12 / 24 / 40 |

Mean w over every acting (state, slot) of the candidate space is the NULL law's mean. In FREE each bit is an independent fair coin, so the means are (N−2)/4 for closure, N−2 for adjacency and (N−2)(N−3)/2 for path. The census reproduces these exactly.

| Component | FREE mean, N=5 / 6 / 7 | Ratio N6→N7 | HELD mean, N=5 / 6 / 7 | Ratio N6→N7 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| closure | 0.75 / 1.00 / 1.25 | 1.25 | 1.18 / 1.38 / 1.58 | 1.15 |
| adjacency | 3.0 / 4.0 / 5.0 | 1.25 | 3.86 / 4.75 / 5.67 | 1.19 |
| path | 3.0 / 6.0 / 10.0 | 1.67 | 5.57 / 9.00 / 13.33 | 1.48 |

**Consequence.** At a fixed W4 grade, the typical path log-weight available to a toggle grows by about 1.5–1.7× from N=6 to N=7. The closure log-weight grows by only about 1.15–1.25×. A composite such as CSPH (closure strong_favour + path weak_favour) therefore changes its *internal balance* as N grows, as well as its overall strength. A fixed grade is not a fixed aggregate influence.

## 3. What the dynamics actually engage (post hoc, published cells)

The null means above are what the representation offers. What matters for a cell is how many witnesses its executed events actually carry under its own stationary law. The new `witness_census_jump` channel measures this, per executed event of each component (`gtobs.witness_census`).

| HELD cell | Component | Engaged mean w, N5 → N6 | Ratio | Null mean ratio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CSPH | closure form (strong_favour) | 0.99 → 0.84 | 0.85 | 1.17 |
| CSPH | path dissolve (weak_favour) | 3.75 → 4.10 | 1.09 | 1.62 |
| CSPF | path form (weak_suppress) | 2.60 → 2.19 | 0.84 | 1.62 |
| CWPH | path dissolve (weak_favour) | 3.13 → 3.44 | 1.10 | 1.62 |
| PATHF weak_suppress | path form | 1.96 → 1.73 | 0.88 | 1.62 |
| PATHH weak_favour | path dissolve | 2.76 → 3.03 | 1.10 | 1.62 |
| CLOSEW (gradient) | closure form (weak_favour) | 2.36 → 3.46 | 1.47 | 1.17 |

FREE cells show the same pattern. Their path-term ratios are 1.20–1.39, against a FREE null ratio of 2.0 from N5 to N6. CLOSEW's is 1.67, and CSPH's closure term falls (0.80 → 0.74).

**Reading.** The non-gradient composites largely regulate themselves away from high-witness states. Their path terms dissolve or suppress the configurations that would carry many witnesses. Their engaged path load grows by about 10% from N5 to N6, against 62% for the null. The engaged closure load in CSPH and CSPF actually falls. The gradient densifier CLOSEW behaves in the opposite way: it walks into dense states, and its engaged load grows faster than the null's.

So witness amplification is not a fixed multiplier attached to N. It depends on the dynamics, and it is measurable. E1 can record the engaged load at N=7 as an ordinary channel, and an interpretation can then condition on it, without assuming it. This is the main reason the confound is partly identifiable (section 6).

Implications for E1:

- **The attachment null r0 falls** from 0.857 to 0.667. A raw margin at N=7 is measured against a lower bar, with more room above it. Comparing raw margins across N mixes a changing ceiling with a changing effect. ## 5. The CSPH margin depends on clock and density (post hoc, published cells)

GT-F26 and the E0 report quote the CSPH margin as +0.047 (N5) and +0.009 (N6). That is the continuous-clock value, attachment_fraction − r0. Recomputing on the published laws gives:

| HELD CSPH | Continuous margin | Continuous, null-density standardised | Jump margin | Jump, null-density standardised |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| N=5 | +0.046 | +0.023 | +0.073 | +0.038 |
| N=6 | +0.009 | **−0.073** | +0.065 | **−0.034** |

- **Clock.** Under the jump clock (per event) the margin hardly shrinks, from +0.073 to +0.065. Its fragility is a property of the per-unit-time convention, which weights long-lived states. Both conventions were published; the report quoted one.
- **Density.** The published profile of attachment fraction by free-edge count k (HELD N6, continuous) is 0.771, 0.792, 0.746, 0.701, 0.667 and 0.650 for k = 1 to 6, against r0 = 0.75. CSPH spends about 93% of its time at k ≤ 3, where the ratio exceeds r0. At typical null densities the same rule mildly favours probe–probe relations. The standardised margin reweights E[a | k] to the null's binomial density profile, and that profile sits where a/k < r0.
- Every comparison cell with a path term (CSPF, CWPH, CWPF, PATHF, PATHH) is negative under both standardisations at N=6.
- **What the standardised margin is.** It is a counterfactual comparison: the rule's conditional preference E[a | k], read at the null's densities. Some of those densities a cell rarely visits. At N=6, k = 9–11 carry about 7% of the binomial weight but can have stationary mass as low as 1e-35. `gtobs` computes those conditionals to about 1e-13 relative, which E0's dense solve did not (validation note, section 3). They still describe configurations the cell does not occupy. The standardised margin therefore complements the raw margin and does not replace it. CLOSEW is mildly positive (+0.03), and NULL is 0 to 1e-12, as the identity requires.

This qualifies GT-F26 without contradicting it. The selective attachment is real at the densities CSPH occupies, but it is a sparse-regime preference, not a density-independent bias toward the source. The qualification comes from a post hoc channel and is recorded as such (coherence ledger, GT-F34). It does not rewrite the published finding.

## 6. Identifiability at N=7

What the native fixed-grade sequence N = 5, 6, 7 (W4) can and cannot separate:

| Possible cause of a change between N=6 and N=7 | Separable at N=7? | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lower attachment ceiling (r0 falls) | Yes | Report raw, normalised and standardised margins together |
| Density shift (the cell visits different k) | Yes | Full a/k profile by k, density-standardised margin, edge-count distribution |
| Clock convention | Yes | Every rate channel in both clocks, as E0 did |
| Witness amplification, overall | Partly | Engaged-witness census at N=7 against N=6, and the base-sensitivity bracket below |
| Witness amplification, component balance (closure vs path) | Only partly | Per-component engaged load. No in-grammar model holds one component's load fixed while N changes |
| Source-share and probe-count changes | No, not from N alone | Intrinsic to HELD with a fixed three-vertex source. A larger held source would be a different instrument (G3) |
| Shell-size and topology changes | Descriptively only | Shell masses against the null shell masses |
| "Intrinsic" size dependence of the organisation | No | The residual after the above. With three sizes and one family it has no unique interpretation |

**A base-sensitivity bracket (within the existing grammar).** The laboratory already defines the sensitivity alphabets W3 (base 3) and W16 (base 4): `weights.py`, `docs/experiment-roadmap.md`, Generation 7. They keep every grade and ordering, and scale every log-factor by log 3 / log 2 = 1.585 or by 2. At a fixed N they change rule strength and nothing else: not the combinatorics, the source share or the shells. Running the same families at N = 5 and 6 under W3 and W16 measures each observable's response to uniform strength scaling at fixed size.

- If an observable's N6→N7 change lies within the span produced by W4→W3→W16 at N6, in the same direction, *and* the N=7 engaged log-weight ratio falls in the 1.0–2.0 range those alphabets bracket, witness amplification remains a candidate explanation.
- If the N=7 change runs opposite to the strength response, or exceeds it while the engaged load barely grows, amplification is unlikely to be the main cause.
- The bracket can be **calibrated on the published N5→N6 step** first. N5 under W16 doubles every log-factor, which exactly matches the path-witness maximum from N5 to N6 (12 × 2 = 24). Comparing N5-W16 with the published N6-W4 tests whether the bracket explains a step whose two ends are already known.

Limits of the bracket:
- It scales closure and path together, so it cannot reproduce the changed closure/path balance of a composite.
- It is a bracket, not a decomposition.
- Exact matching of aggregate log-weight would need non-dyadic bases such as 2^(3/5). The named alphabets exclude these (`formal/expressivity-boundaries.md`), so that would be a grammar change, requiring an ontology proposal, and is not proposed here.
- The single-component families (PATHF weak_suppress, PATHH weak_favour, CLOSEW) are the cleanest bracket cases, because one component carries all the strength.

## 7. What the binary representation does and does not imply

- The count 2^[N(N−1)/2] arises only because this finite model gives each unordered pair one present/absent bit.
- Directed relations, multivalued states, relation types, or triadic (O=3) relations would give different counts and different witness structures.
- The combinatorics are the practical limit on exact exploration: N=8 FREE would have 2^28 ≈ 2.7×10⁸ states.
- No physical or ontological claim about a binary reality follows from this representational choice.

## 8. Predeclared reading rules proposed for E1

These are proposals for the frozen plan, chosen before any N=7 cell is seen:

1. **A sign change of one margin is an observation about that fixed-grade, finite-N model**, in the stated clock and standardisation. It is not on its own evidence of intrinsic size dependence, of witness amplification, or of failure of the wider RS ontology.
2. **Report every margin in four forms**: raw and null-density standardised, each in both clocks. Also report the normalised margin (af − r0)/(1 − r0) and the full a/k profile. No single form is primary for interpretation; the plan may name one form for its frozen expectation, chosen now.
3. **No grade, alphabet or threshold is chosen after seeing N=7.** Any follow-up sensitivity cell is designed and frozen in a later round.
4. **Fragile and negative outcomes are findings.** A vanished margin, a persisting handover with no selectivity, or no effect at all are recorded as computed.

## 4. Pre-freeze algebra (formal note, `docs/e2-formal-mechanism.md`)

The rule definitions above give an exact local identity, verified before freezing on synthetic factor tables only.

- For slots e = (p,q) and f = (p,r) sharing p, the square "form e, form f, dissolve e, dissolve f" from a base state x (where e and f are absent) has log affinity σ·(deg_x(r) − deg_x(q)).
- σ = Σ log m over the path-dissolve components − Σ log m over the path-form components.
- Squares on disjoint slots have affinity 0. Closure and adjacency components cancel.

This turns three of the prompt's live possibilities into precise, separately testable statements:
- **Orientation from signs and incidence.** Locally this is now an identity. Locally the handover is "keep the relation to the better-connected partner, release the one to the poorer". In HELD the source vertices carry two extra neighbours, which explains the observed orientation for σ > 0.
- **Contingent on grading.** Yes, through the sign of σ. Every E1 cell had σ > 0, so the 30/30 invariance is a consequence of the families chosen, not a fact about all path rules.
- **Local affinity against aggregated statistics.** The identity is local. Whether stationary currents and event-order indices follow it, cancel or reverse is **not** implied, and is the open empirical question.

The identity also brings out a **new mechanism**. With a hard path prohibition, no intact square carries affinity (intact squares need deg(r) = deg(q) = 0 for that component). # Formal mechanism note: elementary-square affinities of the GT template grammar

*Prompt GT-P005, deliverable 8.*
- *Sections 1–4 were written before the E2A freeze. They are a pure algebraic derivation, checked on synthetic factor tables (a proof-verification fixture; no round cell).*
- *Section 5 is filled after E2A and E2B and is marked as such.*

## 1. Setting and assumptions

| Item | Assumption |
| --- | --- |
| Grammar | Ordinary pair DSL, order 2, label-covariant templates of `gte0a.component_expressions`: close_form, close_dissolve, adj_form, path_form, path_dissolve |
| Rates | W(x, g) = Π over components of m_c^{w_c(x, g)}, applied to formation (g absent in x) or dissolution (g present) according to the component kind. w_c(x, g) is the number of satisfied instances (witnesses) of component c for slot g in state x |
| Factors | m_c > 0 for the identity; components with m_c = 0 are treated in section 3 |
| Witness counts | w_c(x, g) depends only on slots other than g (template conditions never read g itself) |
| Scaffold | HELD fixes the source triangle (its dissolution has rate 0); those slots never toggle. FREE has no scaffold |
| N, start, clock | Any N ≥ 3. The identity is about rates, so it holds in either clock and does not depend on the start or on the recurrence class |
| Square | For distinct slots e and f and a base state x where both are absent: x → x+e → x+e+f → x+f → x, read as "form e, form f, dissolve e, dissolve f". Its log affinity is A = log[W(x,e) W(x+e,f) W(x+e+f,e) W(x+f,f)] − log[W(x,f) W(x+f,e) W(x+e+f,f) W(x+e,e)] |

## 2. The identity

Write Δ_f w_c(·, e) = w_c(x+f, e) − w_c(x, e). This is how much adding f changes e's witness count. Because witness counts never read e itself, it is the same at x and at x+e.

**Lemma 1 (one component).**
- A formation component contributes log m_c · (Δ_e w_c(·, f) − Δ_f w_c(·, e)).
- A dissolution component contributes log m_c · (Δ_f w_c(·, e) − Δ_e w_c(·, f)).

*Proof.* For a formation component, the forward cycle uses its factor at W(x,e) and W(x+e,f); the reverse uses it at W(x,f) and W(x+f,e). Taking logs, the difference is log m · [w(x,e) + w(x+e,f) − w(x,f) − w(x+f,e)] = log m · [Δ_e w(·,f) − Δ_f w(·,e)]. Dissolution is the same with the cycle's dissolve steps, with the opposite sign. ∎

**Lemma 2 (cross-counts).** Let e = (p,q) and f = (p,r) share exactly vertex p.
- **Closure:** Δ_f w(·,e) = Δ_e w(·,f) = [q~r]. The only new witness is the vertex at the far end of the other slot, which needs the edge (q,r).
- **Adjacency:** Δ_f w(·,e) = Δ_e w(·,f) = 1.
- **Path:** Δ_f w(·,e) = |N_x(r) \ {q}| and Δ_e w(·,f) = |N_x(q) \ {r}|.
  - The new witnesses of e created by f are the paths p–r–d with d ∈ N(r), d ∉ {p,q}.
  - f cannot be the (c,d) link of a witness of e, because c, d ∉ {p,q} would exclude p.
  - p ∉ N_x(r), since f is absent in x.

For disjoint slots e = (a,b) and f = (c,d), every component kind gives Δ_f w(·,e) = Δ_e w(·,f):
- closure gives 0;
- adjacency gives 0;
- path gives the number of present edges between {a,b} and {c,d}, which is symmetric.

**Theorem (square affinity).** Under the assumptions of section 1, with all factors positive:
- if e = (p,q) and f = (p,r) share p, then A = σ · (deg_x(r) − deg_x(q));
- if e and f are disjoint, then A = 0.

Here σ = Σ_{path_dissolve c} log m_c − Σ_{path_form c} log m_c.

*Proof.* Combine the lemmas. Closure and adjacency cross-counts are symmetric, so they cancel. For path components, |N_x(r) \ {q}| − |N_x(q) \ {r}| = deg_x(r) − deg_x(q), because the term [q~r] cancels. ∎

**Corollaries.**
1. **Reversibility.** A rule with σ = 0 has zero affinity on every elementary square.
   - When every non-scaffold toggle has positive rate, the class is a subcube. The cycle space of a hypercube graph is generated by its 4-cycles, so Kolmogorov's criterion holds and the chain is reversible.
   - This covers every positive-factor gradient family (GT-F12) and PCOMP (GT-F30). It predicts the same for the untested pair path_form weak_suppress + path_dissolve weak_suppress.
   - For classes restricted by hard components (not subcubes), squares need not generate all cycles, so reversibility needs a separate argument. For a gradient restriction such as EXCL, the restricted Gibbs law satisfies detailed balance directly, because forward and reverse rates are zero together.
2. **Orientation rule.**
   - The cycle that forms the relation to the better-connected far endpoint second and dissolves the relation to the poorer one first is favoured exactly when σ > 0. Its log affinity equals σ times the degree difference.
   - In words: when σ > 0, the relation to the poorer-connected partner is released while the relation to the richer is kept. When σ < 0 it is the reverse.
3. **HELD handover.** Take an attachment/probe square with shared probe p, far endpoints a source vertex s and a probe q.
   - deg_x(s) ≥ 2, because of the two other source vertices.
   - At N=5, deg_x(q) ≤ 2: the only possible neighbours besides p are the other source vertices besides s.
   - So deg(s) − deg(q) ≥ 0, and every such square has the sign of σ. Reversed attachment/probe squares are impossible at HELD N=5 and possible from N=6.
4. **Scope of the E1 invariance.** Every E0B/E1 family has σ = +log 2 (path_form weak_suppress or path_dissolve weak_favour, plus closure). The 30/30 invariance is therefore the case σ > 0 of this identity, *at the level of local rates*. The identity alone does not show that stationary currents follow.

## 3. Hard components (factor 0)

A component with m_c = 0 sets the rate to 0 wherever it reads a witness. A square is *intact* when all eight rates are positive.
- On an intact square, that component reads no witness at any of the four states. That forces its cross-counts to 0, so its contribution is 0, and the identity holds with σ computed over the positive-factor components.
- **Path prohibition** (path_form or path_dissolve with factor 0): an intact square needs deg(r) = deg(q) = 0 among the relevant vertices, so every intact square has A = 0.
- **One-way transitions.** These arise where a transition is admissible and its reverse is not. With one-way transitions, Kolmogorov's criterion fails on cycles that are not elementary squares, or on broken squares. Irreversibility can then exist with zero affinity on every intact square.
  - Synthetic check: FREE N=4 path_form prohibit has irreversible flux 0.12 and 48 one-way transitions, with no intact square carrying affinity.
  - Entropy production is infinite in that case, and `gte0a.reversibility` excludes such pairs from its sum.

## 4. What is not claimed

- **No statement about stationary currents.** The theorem says nothing about how the currents distribute over squares, about aggregated event-order indices, or about frames. Those are E2A observables.
- **No physical statement.** This is ordinary Markov-chain cycle structure (Kolmogorov's criterion, Schnakenberg's cycle decomposition) applied to a declared grammar. It is not a physical arrow, and it is not entropy production in any physical substrate.
- **Not a theorem outside its assumptions.** For example, it does not cover rules reading three-relation conditions beyond the listed templates, history, or directed relations.

## 5. Results after E2A and E2B (written after the rounds)

**5.1 The identity on every executed cell [M, O].** I1 and I2 hold in all 64 executed cells: 46 in E2A and 18 in E2B. Across all four strata the largest residual is about 1e-15. The affinity was recomputed independently from the rule strings with exact fractions, on 120 seeded squares per cell, and agreed to 1e-12 or better. The census is evidence within its coverage; the identity itself is proved in section 2.

**5.2 Aggregated orientation versus σ (empirical, not proved) [O].**
- In every cell with only positive factors and σ ≠ 0, the signs agree: 32 E2A cells and 4 E2B cells (hard closure exclusion with σ < 0). The quantities compared are σ, the partner-frame index and (HELD) the handover index. One E2A cell lies below the 1e-12 reporting floor.
- No proof is offered that the stationary aggregate must take σ's sign. Square-level circulation runs against local affinity on 6–36% of the circulation mass, so a proof would have to work at the level of the whole cycle decomposition.
- **Counterexample when one-way transitions are present.** Take hard path-form prohibition plus path_dissolve weak_suppress (σ = −log 2, FREE N=5). Its partner index is **+0.070**, opposite to σ. The cell's irreversibility comes mostly from 510 one-way transitions, not from intact squares. The σ rule's domain is therefore chains without one-way transitions.

**5.3 Hard adjacency exclusion makes path terms inert (theorem) [M].**
- Under adj_form prohibit from a start with no adjacent pair, forming (a,b) is admissible only when a and b both have no neighbours. Every reachable state is therefore a matching.
- A path witness needs two present edges sharing a vertex, so every path witness count is 0 and every path component's factor is 1.
- So adj_form prohibit combined with any path term gives exactly the same chain as adj_form prohibit alone. That chain is a gradient restriction and reversible.
- Observed: all five such E2B cells per mode have identical laws (flux 8e-16, expected relations 1.54), and strict enabling (60%) without any direction.

**5.4 The held source is a witness (theorem) [M].**
- In HELD, every attachment slot (p,s) has the two-path s–s'–s'' inside the source triangle. Under path_form prohibit no attachment can ever form.
- Every source vertex has neighbours, so under adj_form prohibit no relation touching the source can form.
- In both cases HELD reduces to the probe-only subgraph: two states at N=5, with one probe–probe slot.
- The imposed reference is not neutral to hard rules.

**5.5 One-way transitions under hard path-form prohibition [M, O].**
- Formation of (a,b) is forbidden while a or b is the end of a two-path; dissolution is unrestricted. So the one-way transitions are exactly the **releases** of relations whose re-formation is currently forbidden.
- Observed: 100% of one-way flux is dissolution (FREE N=5), and it is 5.6–7.3% of total flux.
